summary: Specifies the TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO), which replaces the TCP MD5 Signature option of RFC 2385. It supports stronger message authentication codes, protects against replay on long-lived connections, and works with static or externally managed keys. It suits uses like BGP and LDP. It is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: A secret handshake stamped on every TCP message so no one can fake them. It is a newer and stronger stamp than the old one.
